conviction.explanation: Underlying hospital profit/EBITDA growth provides a substantive upside case, but 30.38x trailing earnings, material net debt and RM141m conservative cash against RM486m dividends leave owner-return compensation balanced. Growth has not yet delivered financial repair.

executive_summary:
IHH has real underlying operating progress: excluding MFRS129, revenue grew 7% and EBITDA14%, while H1 ex-exceptional profit rose 22%. RM771m pre-financing FCF confirms investment is producing some cash beyond accounting growth.

After specified finance and lease costs, H1 cash was only RM141m against RM486m owner dividends. Net debt of RM11.564bn excludes RM2.205bn leases, and 30.38x trailing earnings requires sustained delivery. Neutral balances growth with current conversion pressure and a weak trend; unresolved governance statements support no invented legal conclusion.
bull_case: Profitable hospital growth could improve cash conversion and reduce debt reliance if more cash is retained.
bear_case: Capital intensity, payouts and financing costs could prevent growth reaching shareholders; admissions weakness and governance uncertainty constrain extrapolation.
key_uncertainties: Cash conversion after capital investment, finance costs and leases.
Dividend restraint or retained-cash repair is prospective.
Outcome of inaccessible legal/governance statements remains unknown.
catalysts_upcoming: Comparable cash after the same deductions covering owner dividends with stable/lower net debt would strengthen owner economics.
Continued underlying EBITDA/profit growth alongside admissions recovery would support productive expansion.
